claim.quote: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

date.note: arXiv submission date (v1, 23 July 2001). Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 87, 091802 (2001); the exact journal publication date was not read.

name: Observation of large CP violation in the neutral B meson system
notes: Companion measurement to BaBar's contemporaneous result; that is not recorded here.

significance.quote: A zero value for sin 2φ1 is ruled out at a level greater than 6σ.
significance.value: more than 6σ (a zero value of sin 2φ₁ is ruled out)

summary.plain: Belle measured how the decay-time distributions of neutral B particles and their antiparticles differ for certain final states, and found a large asymmetry (sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14 ± 0.06). The collaboration concluded that it had observed CP violation, a matter–antimatter asymmetry, in the neutral B meson system, and ruled out a zero value at more than 6σ.
summary.technical: Time-dependent measurement of the CP asymmetry with 29.1 fb^-1 at the Υ(4S), one B⁰ fully reconstructed as J/ψ K_S, ψ(2S) K_S, χ_c1 K_S, η_c K_S, J/ψ K_L or J/ψ K*⁰ and the flavour of the other identified from its decay products: sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14 (stat) ± 0.06 (syst). 'We conclude that we have observed CP violation in the neutral B meson system'; a zero value of sin 2φ₁ is ruled out at a level greater than 6σ.

title: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System
why_it_matters: The paper explains that the Kobayashi–Maskawa model predicts large CP violation in certain B-meson decays, so that measurements of CP violation in B meson decays provide important tests of the KM model; it reports that the result is consistent with the higher range of values allowed by the constraints of the KM model.
